practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word profile of a fictional student. Include an interest, a specific experience, its significance, and a realistic learning goal.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構學生，包含興趣、一段具體經驗、經驗的意義及實際可行的學習目標。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy enjoys explaining how everyday objects work. Last term, she helped a younger student repair a bicycle light. She discovered that a simple drawing made her instructions easier to follow. That experience encouraged her to join the design club. She now wants to improve her drawing skills and test her explanations with classmates. Her goal is to create a short repair guide that a beginner can actually use.
practice.reading_en: Sam is a new member of the school media club. He enjoys photography, but his interest is not only in attractive pictures. Last spring, he photographed the school garden while volunteers were replacing broken signs. A younger student later told him that the pictures explained the work more clearly than a list of tasks. Sam began to notice how images could help people understand a process. This term, he wants to create a photo guide for new garden volunteers. He plans to ask a beginner to follow the guide before sharing it with the club. For Sam, a successful picture is one that helps someone act.

questions.prompt_en: What does Sam want to create this term?
questions.answer_en: He wants to create a photo guide for new garden volunteers.

questions.prompt_en: How did the younger student's comment influence Sam?
questions.answer_en: It helped him recognize that photographs could explain a process, not just look attractive.

questions.prompt_en: Why is asking a beginner to follow the guide a sensible test?
questions.answer_en: His guide is for new volunteers, so a beginner can show whether the pictures explain what to do.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word update on a fictional school project. Include a finished past event, progress up to now, and one task still remaining.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構校園專題進度，包含已結束的過去事件、截至目前的進展及一項尚待完成的工作。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our class started a reading corner last month. We moved two shelves into an empty classroom and invited students to suggest books. Since then, we have collected enough stories for the first shelf. Several younger students have visited the corner, but we have not opened it every day yet. We still need to agree on a schedule. The first visits gave us useful questions to discuss at our next meeting.
practice.reading_en: Last term, Amy joined a team that was designing a quieter lunch area. The team interviewed students in May and presented its first plan in June. Since then, the school has provided a small room, and volunteers have moved some tables into it. Amy has written a short welcome notice, but the team has not agreed on opening hours yet. The room is ready for a trial, not for a permanent opening. Amy says the earlier interviews helped the team choose the location. She believes the next step is to watch how students use the room during a short trial and then review the schedule.

questions.prompt_en: What work has the team not finished yet?
questions.answer_en: It has not agreed on opening hours.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the passage use interviewed with in May but has provided with since then?
questions.answer_en: In May identifies a finished past time; since then links later progress to the present.

questions.prompt_en: Would it be accurate to announce that the room is permanently open? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. It is only ready for a trial, and the opening hours have not been agreed.

titles.ja: 活動が続いている時間

objectives_zh_TW: 用 have 或 has been 加 ing 描述持續至今的活動。
以 for、since 交代期間或起點，辨認最近活動的當下跡象。
比較活動歷程與已完成成果，避免把進行式等同完成。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 問自己句子強調「做了多久」還是「完成多少」；持續練習不代表已完成一場演出。

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word update about a fictional student learning a skill. Explain the duration, current evidence, and a result that is not yet complete.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構學生學習技能的近況，說明持續時間、現在可觀察的跡象及尚未完成的成果。
practice.sample_answer_en: Sam has been practicing the guitar for three months. Since the start of the term, he has been meeting a friend after school to work on difficult changes between notes. His fingers are sore today because he has been practicing a new song. He can now play its opening smoothly, but he has not learned the whole piece yet. He plans to record another practice session and listen for places that need attention.
practice.reading_en: For the past two weeks, Amy has been preparing a short talk for the science club. She has been practicing in an empty classroom since Monday because the library is busy. Today her voice sounds tired, and several pages of notes are spread across a desk. She has been rehearsing the opening, but she has not decided how to explain the final experiment. Her partner suggests another picture instead of another paragraph. Amy stops practicing to draw it. Although she is no longer speaking at this moment, the tired voice and notes still show evidence of her recent work. The talk itself is not finished.

questions.prompt_en: Why does her tired voice support the description of recent activity?
questions.answer_en: The passage says she has been rehearsing, which explains the tired voice even after she stops.

questions.prompt_en: Does has been preparing prove that the talk is complete? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. It emphasizes the activity, and the text says she has not decided how to explain the final experiment.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word account of a fictional school event. Begin with a past problem, explain an earlier action using the past perfect, and describe the outcome.

practice.sample_answer_en: When the drama team arrived, the classroom door was locked. Sam checked his bag, but the key was missing. He had lent it to Amy that morning because she needed to collect some costumes. Fortunately, Amy had left the key with the school office before lunch. Sam went there and collected it. The team started rehearsal a little late, but the earlier arrangement prevented a much longer delay.
practice.reading_en: When Sam opened the presentation file at two, several pictures were missing. He thought the team would need to rebuild the whole slideshow. Amy, however, had saved a complete copy on another computer before lunch. She had noticed a problem with the classroom computer that morning and had decided to make a backup. The team copied her file and tested it. By three, the pictures were working again. In his report, Sam described the missing pictures first because that was the problem he had seen. He then explained Amy's earlier actions. The order of his report was different from the order in which the events had happened.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word plan for a fictional group project. State an activity in progress at a future time, a result completed by a deadline, and one condition that could affect the plan.

practice.sample_answer_en: Our group is preparing a short film for Friday. At three tomorrow, Amy will be checking the sound while Sam reviews the final scene. If another group needs it, we may need to move the sound check to a different room.
practice.reading_en: The media club is preparing a film for the school exhibition. According to its plan, the members will be editing the final scene at four on Thursday. By five, they will have completed the film and saved two copies. They will then test the film in the exhibition room. Sam warns that finishing the file does not guarantee that the room's speakers will work. The team therefore allows an extra hour for the test. At six, they expect to be ready to leave. Their plan describes intended progress, not a promise that no problems can occur. If the equipment fails, they will review the schedule.

objectives_zh_TW: 用限定關係子句辨認所指的人或物。
比較關係詞作主詞與受詞時的句子角色。
在本課限定子句中適當省略受詞關係詞，保留主詞關係詞。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先讀關係詞後面：若已有 Amy 這類主詞，關係詞可能是受詞；不要只看到 who 或 that 就一律省略。

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word description of a fictional school team. Use a defining relative clause with a subject relative word and one with an object relative word. Explain why a particular person or resource is suitable.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構校園團隊，使用一個關係詞作主詞的限定子句和一個作受詞的限定子句，並解釋特定人物或資源為何合適。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our team needs a student who can explain simple repairs patiently. Amy is a good choice because she helped new volunteers last term. The guide that she wrote uses pictures instead of long paragraphs. We also need someone who can test the instructions without extra help. Sam can do that because he has not used the equipment before. His questions will show us which parts of the guide need clearer explanations.
practice.reading_en: The garden club needs volunteers for two different jobs. Students who enjoy working outdoors can help repair signs. Students who prefer writing can improve the volunteer guide. Amy offers to work on the guide that Sam wrote last term. She thinks the photographs are useful, but some instructions are difficult to follow. The student who tests the revised guide should be new to the garden. An experienced volunteer might understand an unclear instruction simply because they already know the task. The club therefore asks Pip, a new member, to try the guide. His questions help the writers identify information that a beginner needs.

questions.prompt_en: Which job is offered to students who prefer writing?
questions.answer_en: They can improve the volunteer guide.

questions.prompt_en: In the guide that Sam wrote, who performs the writing?
questions.answer_en: Sam performs the writing; that refers to the guide as the object of wrote.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the club want a beginner to test the guide?
questions.answer_en: An experienced volunteer might understand unclear instructions from prior knowledge, while a beginner can reveal missing information.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word update about a fictional club. Introduce a named person and an identified object with non-defining relative clauses. Include one defining clause that identifies a smaller group.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹虛構社團近況，用非限定關係子句補充已具名人物及已知物品的資訊，另用限定子句指出較小的一群人。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy, who leads our media club, is preparing an exhibition. Our main camera, which the school bought last year, is ready to use. Students who have finished their captions can help arrange the photographs. Others still need to check names and dates. Sam, who enjoys organizing displays, has offered to plan the entrance. These different roles allow everyone to contribute without pretending that every part of the exhibition is already finished.
practice.reading_en: Amy leads a small media club with three members: Sam, Pip, and herself. Amy, who joined the club last year, now organizes its exhibition. She writes two possible notices. The first says, "Students who have finished their captions can arrange the display." This notice invites only the students with completed captions. The second says, "The students, who have finished their captions, can arrange the display." In that notice, all the students being discussed have finished. Amy chooses the first because Pip is still checking a date. The main camera, which Sam borrowed from the office, is ready. Their preparations are progressing, but the members are not all at the same stage.

questions.prompt_en: Why does Amy choose the first notice?
questions.answer_en: Pip is still checking a date, so only students with finished captions should arrange the display.

questions.prompt_en: How do the commas change the meaning of the second notice?
questions.answer_en: They make having finished the captions extra information about all the students being discussed.

questions.prompt_en: Would the second notice accurately describe this group now? Support your answer.
questions.answer_en: No. It presents all the students as finished, but Pip is still checking a date.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word notice for a fictional school event. Include one active description using an ing form and one passive description using a past participle. Make the location and required action clear.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞寫虛構校園活動公告，包含一個 ing 主動描述和一個過去分詞被動描述，清楚交代地點與必要行動。
practice.sample_answer_en: Students waiting for the design workshop should meet outside Room Eight. The forms printed yesterday are on the table beside the door. Please take one form and check your group number before entering. A student carrying a blue folder will answer questions about the schedule. The equipment borrowed from the science club is for the afternoon session, so please leave it on the shelves until the teacher gives further instructions.
practice.reading_en: The design club is preparing a notice for a workshop. Its first draft says, "Students who are waiting outside should collect the forms that were printed yesterday." Amy revises this to "Students waiting outside should collect the forms printed yesterday." The shorter version keeps the same basic meaning: the students are doing the waiting, while the forms received the printing action. She also adds the location of the forms, a table beside Room Eight. Sam suggests shortening every sentence, but Amy disagrees. A shorter notice is useful only if readers still know who should act and what they should do. They test the notice with a student who has not attended before.

questions.prompt_en: Where can students find the forms?
questions.answer_en: On a table beside Room Eight.

questions.prompt_en: Why does waiting describe the students but printed describe the forms?
questions.answer_en: The students perform the waiting, while the forms receive the printing action.

questions.prompt_en: Why does Amy reject shortening every sentence automatically?
questions.answer_en: She wants readers to know who should act and what to do; being shorter alone does not guarantee clarity.

objectives_zh_TW: 把 that 或 wh 子句作為句子中的完整資訊單位。

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word paragraph about improving a fictional school service. Use a that clause as an object and a what or how clause as a subject. Explain one observation and one question still needing an answer.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞說明如何改善虛構校園服務，使用 that 子句作受詞及 what 或 how 子句作主詞，交代一項觀察和一個待解問題。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our team noticed that several students arrived at the wrong room for tutoring. What they need is a notice with a clear room number. The current notice gives the day and time but leaves out the location. We do not know why the number was removed, so we should ask the organizer before changing the file. How students find the notice also matters, because an accurate message is useful only if they can see it.
practice.reading_en: The student council is reviewing its tutoring notice. Amy explains that several new students went to the library instead of Room Five. What confused them was a missing room number, not the starting time. Sam checks the original message and confirms that it gives Tuesday at four but no location. The team wants to know why the room number disappeared from the final version. They cannot answer that question from the notice alone. How students receive the message also matters: some see a printed copy, while others read it on a phone. The council decides to check both versions before announcing a correction, so that the same mistake does not remain in one format.

questions.prompt_en: What information was missing from the notice?
questions.answer_en: The room number was missing.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the council check both the printed and phone versions?
questions.answer_en: Students receive the notice in both formats, so correcting only one could leave the mistake in the other.

questions.prompt_en: Can the council conclude who removed the room number? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The notice shows the missing information but does not explain why it disappeared or who removed it.

objectives_zh_TW: 把直接問句改為嵌入式問句並保持敘述語序。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 客氣開頭後仍要有明確問題；檢查 embedded clause 中的主詞動詞順序，也檢查收件者知道你要什麼。

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word email to a fictional school organizer. Explain your context, ask two specific embedded questions, and close politely without assuming approval.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞寫信給虛構校園活動負責人，交代背景、提出兩個具體嵌入式問句，並客氣結尾，不預設已獲許可。
practice.sample_answer_en: Dear Ms. Lee, Our media club is preparing photographs for the school exhibition next Friday. Could you tell me whether the spare camera is available on Thursday afternoon? I would also like to know where we should return it after use. We need it for indoor pictures and can collect it after our last class. Thank you for considering our request. We will wait for your reply before changing our plan. Best regards, Amy
practice.reading_en: Amy wants to borrow a camera for the school exhibition. Her first message says only, "Can we have the camera?" The organizer cannot tell which camera she means or when the club needs it. Amy revises the message. She explains that the club is taking indoor photographs on Thursday afternoon. She then asks, "Could you tell me whether the spare camera is available then?" A second question asks where the camera should be returned. The new message is polite, but its usefulness also comes from the specific details. Amy has not received permission yet, so she keeps another plan available and waits for the organizer's reply.

questions.prompt_en: What two details were unclear in Amy's first message?
questions.answer_en: Which camera she meant and when the club needed it.

questions.prompt_en: Why is the revised request easier for the organizer to answer?
questions.answer_en: It identifies the spare camera, gives Thursday afternoon, and asks a specific availability question.

questions.prompt_en: Does a polite request mean Amy may take the camera immediately? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. She has not received permission and is waiting for the organizer's reply.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word profile of a fictional student applying for a club role. Connect an earlier difficulty, a specific response, and a current goal. Include a claim supported by the experience.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞介紹申請社團職務的虛構學生，連結較早遇到的困難、具體回應與目前目標，並提出有該經驗支持的看法。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy hopes to help train new members of the design club. Last term, a student could not follow the instructions she had written. Instead of blaming the reader, Amy watched the student try each step and added clearer labels. She has since been testing her guides with beginners before sharing them. This experience suggests that she is willing to revise her work in response to feedback. She now wants to make the club handbook easier to use.
practice.reading_en: Sam is applying to help organize the school exhibition. His profile begins with a mistake: last year, he placed several captions beside the wrong photographs. A visitor pointed out the problem, and Sam checked every label before the next group arrived. Since then, he has been using a numbered plan when arranging displays. He also asks another student to compare the plan with the finished arrangement. In his application, Sam says this experience taught him to check information rather than trust his memory. He now wants to help new club members prepare their first display. The profile supports a claim about careful improvement, but it does not show that Sam can manage every part of a large event alone.

questions.prompt_en: What role is Sam applying for?
questions.answer_en: He is applying to help organize the school exhibition.

questions.prompt_en: How did Sam change his preparation after the earlier mistake?
questions.answer_en: He began using a numbered plan and asking another student to check the arrangement against it.

questions.prompt_en: Is the claim that Sam can manage every part of a large event alone supported? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The profile shows improved checking of displays, but gives no evidence about managing every event task alone.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90-word connected profile of a fictional student. Link a past experience, ongoing learning, and a future goal. Include one relative clause and one noun clause, and keep claims supported by details.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用六十至九十詞寫虛構學生的連貫介紹，連結過去經驗、持續學習及未來目標，包含一個關係子句與一個名詞子句，並以細節支持看法。
practice.sample_answer_en: Amy, who enjoys explaining practical skills, wants to help new science club members. Last term, she discovered that her instructions were unclear when a beginner followed the wrong step. She has been testing her guides with new readers since then. The comments she collects help her identify missing information. What she values most is seeing someone complete a task independently. By the next club meeting, she will have revised the guide for one simple experiment.
practice.reading_en: Pip is preparing a profile for the school design club. His first draft lists several interests but does not explain how they connect. He revises it around one experience. Last term, a new student struggled to follow a map that Pip had drawn. Pip asked where the student had become confused and changed the labels. Since then, he has been testing his maps with people who do not know the building. What he wants to learn next is how to make directions clearer without adding too much text. By the club interview, he expects to have completed a revised map. His profile now connects a problem, a response, continuing practice, and a realistic goal.

questions.prompt_en: What problem led Pip to revise his map?
questions.answer_en: A new student struggled to follow it.

questions.prompt_en: How does the revised profile improve on the first draft?
questions.answer_en: It connects one experience to his response, continuing practice, and goal instead of listing unrelated interests.

questions.prompt_en: Would adding a claim that everyone can now follow Pip's maps be justified? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. He is still testing them, and the passage does not report that every reader succeeds.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words proposing one focused improvement to a school space. Begin with a topic sentence and support only its controlling idea.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，建議改善校園的一個空間。以主題句開頭，後續細節只支持該句的中心想法。
practice.sample_answer_en: A quiet reading hour would make our library more useful for independent study. After lunch, students often need to finish a short assignment before class. A clearly marked quiet area would let them work without nearby conversations. Librarians could explain the rule at the entrance and direct group discussions to another table. These simple changes would give students a dependable place to concentrate during a busy school day.
practice.reading_en: Sunny is writing a paragraph for a fictional school newsletter. Her first topic is the library, but that subject could include books, computers, opening hours, and building design. She narrows her focus to a quiet reading hour after lunch. Her new topic sentence explains how this hour could improve concentration. She supports it with observations about conversations near the entrance and students searching for peaceful places to finish assignments. A sentence about the library's colorful anniversary poster does not develop that idea, so she saves it for another article. The revised paragraph gives readers one clear point to follow.

questions.prompt_en: What improvement does Sunny focus on?
questions.answer_en: She focuses on a quiet reading hour after lunch.

questions.prompt_en: Why does she remove the sentence about the anniversary poster?
questions.answer_en: It does not explain how the quiet hour could improve concentration.

questions.prompt_en: Would a detail about students finishing assignments in a quiet area fit? Explain.
questions.answer_en: Yes. It would directly support the controlling idea that the quiet hour improves concentration.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words supporting a refill station near a school gym. Include a reason, an explicitly fictional example, an explanation, and a limit on the evidence.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，支持在體育館旁設補水站。包含理由、明示虛構的例子、例子的解釋，以及證據的限制。
practice.sample_answer_en: A refill station near the gym could save time between lessons. In a fictional class example, Mina walks to the cafeteria tap and spends five minutes away from the changing room. This delay leaves her less time to prepare for her next lesson. A nearby tap could shorten that walk. However, one example cannot show how often the problem occurs. The school should observe more students before choosing a location.
practice.reading_en: Pip proposes a refill station near the school gym. His first draft says only that the station would be useful. To strengthen the paragraph, he explains that the current tap requires a long walk to the cafeteria. He adds a fictional example: after a sports lesson, Mina spends five minutes reaching the tap and returning. Pip then explains that this trip reduces her time to change before the next class. He does not claim that every student has the same experience. Instead, he suggests observing several classes to learn whether the delay is common. The example illustrates his reason while the final sentence acknowledges a limit.

questions.prompt_en: Where is the current tap in Pip's proposal?
questions.answer_en: It is in the cafeteria.

questions.prompt_en: How does the Mina example support the proposal?
questions.answer_en: It shows how the walk to the tap can reduce time for changing before class.

questions.prompt_en: Does the example prove that every student needs a new station? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. It describes one fictional student; Pip suggests observing several classes to see whether the delay is common.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words about a club changing from paper to digital notices. Use one addition, one contrast, and one result connector, plus a clear this + noun reference.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，說明社團把紙本通知改為數位通知。使用增加、對比、結果連接詞各一個，以及清楚的 this 加名詞指代。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our club now posts its weekly notices on a shared page. This change lets members check meeting times from home. In addition, the page keeps older notices in one place. However, some students cannot check their phones during the school day. We will therefore keep one printed copy beside the classroom door. The two formats can work together, giving members useful access without covering the whole noticeboard with paper.
practice.reading_en: The drama club is revising a paragraph about digital notices. The first sentence explains that a shared page lets members check meeting times at home. The next sentence adds another benefit: older notices remain available. A third sentence introduces a problem because some members cannot use phones at school. Finally, the club proposes keeping a printed copy beside the classroom door. Sunny chooses In addition for the second benefit, However for the problem, and Therefore for the response. She removes a second result connector from the last sentence. She also replaces a vague This with This change so readers can identify the move to digital notices.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the club keep a printed copy?
questions.answer_en: Some members cannot use phones at school.

questions.prompt_en: What relationship does However mark in the paragraph?
questions.answer_en: It introduces a limitation that contrasts with the benefits of digital notices.

questions.prompt_en: Why is This change clearer than This here?
questions.answer_en: It identifies the move to digital notices as the idea being discussed, rather than leaving the reference vague.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words comparing a school hall and courtyard for a book fair. Compare at least two shared criteria, choose a venue, and acknowledge its limitation.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，比較禮堂與中庭作為書展場地。用至少兩個共同標準比較，選出一處並承認它的限制。
practice.sample_answer_en: The courtyard and school hall are both available for our book fair. The courtyard offers more space for visitors, while the hall has fewer seats. However, the hall protects books from rain, whereas the courtyard has no roof. Both places have entrances that students can reach easily. I recommend the hall because protecting donated books matters more than extra seating for this event. We could manage its limited space by admitting smaller groups.
practice.reading_en: A fictional student committee compares the school hall and courtyard for a book fair. Rather than listing unrelated advantages, members choose three shared criteria: space, weather protection, and access. The courtyard provides more room for visitors, but it has no roof. The hall is smaller, yet its roof protects the books from rain. Both entrances are easy to reach from classrooms. The committee expects visitors to arrive in small groups, so extra space is less important than keeping donated books dry. Members choose the hall and explain this priority in their paragraph. They still acknowledge that a much larger event might need the courtyard.

questions.prompt_en: What three criteria does the committee use?
questions.answer_en: It compares space, weather protection, and access.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the committee give weather protection more weight than space?
questions.answer_en: Visitors are expected in small groups, while donated books need protection from rain.

questions.prompt_en: Would the hall necessarily be best for every event? Use the text.
questions.answer_en: No. The text notes that a much larger event might need the courtyard's extra space.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words about a fictional lunch queue that shortened after an early menu sign and extra volunteers were introduced. Explain a possible mechanism and a causal limitation.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，描述虛構午餐排隊在提早展示菜單並增派志工後縮短。解釋可能作用方式及因果判斷的限制。
practice.sample_answer_en: In a fictional school trial, the lunch queue became shorter after a menu sign was placed near the entrance. Students could choose their meals before reaching the counter, which may have reduced questions during service. However, extra volunteers also joined the lunch team that week. The shorter queue therefore cannot be attributed to the sign alone. A later comparison with the same number of volunteers could help the school understand the sign's contribution.
practice.reading_en: In a fictional school trial, a menu sign is moved from the lunch counter to the entrance. Observers notice that students read it while waiting and arrive at the counter with a choice ready. Fewer students ask the server to describe the meals. The queue becomes shorter during the trial week. However, extra volunteers also help serve food during that week. Sunny writes that the sign may have reduced questions, which could have helped the queue move. She does not say the sign was the only cause. To examine that claim, the school would need a fairer comparison that keeps volunteer numbers similar.

questions.prompt_en: Why can Sunny not identify the sign as the only cause?

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words explaining a fictional school book-exchange process. Give ordered steps, name an important worker, and use both active and passive sentences clearly.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，說明虛構校園換書流程。依序列步驟，指出重要負責者，清楚使用主動句和被動句。
practice.sample_answer_en: First, students leave donated books on the collection table. A volunteer checks each book for missing pages before it enters the exchange. Books with serious damage are placed in a separate box for repair. Next, the accepted books are labeled by genre so visitors can find suitable titles. Finally, volunteers arrange them on the display shelves. Naming the checker makes responsibility clear, while the passive sentences keep attention on how the books are handled.
practice.reading_en: The student council is preparing instructions for a fictional book exchange. Students first leave donations on a collection table. A volunteer checks each book for missing pages and loose covers. Books needing repairs are placed in a separate box, while usable books receive genre labels. The labeled books are then arranged on display shelves. Pip notices that an early draft placed labeling before inspection, which could waste labels on unusable books. He changes the order. He also names the volunteer responsible for checking, but uses passive sentences when the books themselves are the main focus. The finished instructions tell readers both what happens and who handles the crucial check.

objectives_zh_TW: 在 although 後使用完整子句，在 despite 後使用名詞或 ing。
用具體優點與限制平衡同一個段落。
以對比連接支持評估，不把缺點隱藏在結論中。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先看連接詞後面的形式：although 後有主詞與動詞；本課 despite 後接名詞片語或 ing 形式。

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words evaluating a small school garden. Include a useful activity and a limitation, using although with a clause and despite with a noun phrase or ing form.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，評估小型校園花園。包含有用活動與限制，使用 although 加子句及 despite 加名詞片語或 ing 形式。
practice.sample_answer_en: Although our school garden is small, it gives students a place to observe living plants closely. Science classes can measure growth and compare leaves instead of relying only on pictures. Despite its educational value, the garden cannot hold a whole year group at once because the paths are narrow. It also needs regular care during holidays. We should keep using it with small classes and arrange a clear watering schedule so its benefits remain practical.
practice.reading_en: The school garden committee is preparing a balanced paragraph for a fictional planning meeting. The garden is small, but students use it to measure plant growth and sketch leaves for art lessons. These activities connect classroom ideas with direct observation. The committee also identifies limits. Narrow paths make large group visits difficult, and plants need care during school holidays. Its paragraph begins with Although the garden is small to acknowledge the first concern before explaining the benefits. Later, Despite its educational value introduces a genuine practical problem. The conclusion recommends keeping the garden for small classes while arranging a holiday watering schedule, rather than pretending the limits do not exist.

questions.prompt_en: Name two learning activities offered by the garden.
questions.answer_en: Students measure plant growth and sketch leaves for art lessons.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the committee mention narrow paths and holiday care?
questions.answer_en: They show practical limits that must be addressed in a balanced evaluation.

questions.prompt_en: Does the committee's recommendation ignore the problems? Explain with evidence.
questions.answer_en: No. It limits visits to small classes and recommends a holiday watering schedule.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words explaining fictional workshop access. Use unless and provided that, then explain why meeting the supervision condition does not guarantee every session will happen.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，說明虛構工作坊使用規定。使用 unless 與 provided that，並解釋符合監督條件為何不保證每次活動都舉行。
practice.sample_answer_en: The school workshop will remain closed unless a teacher is present. Students may use its tools provided that the teacher supervises their work. These rules make supervision necessary, but they do not promise that every supervised session will happen. If essential equipment is damaged, the session may still be canceled. Before bringing a project, students should check both the teacher's availability and the workshop notice. Clear conditions help everyone plan without assuming permission is automatic.
practice.reading_en: A fictional school workshop posts an access notice. It says the room will remain closed unless a teacher is present. Students may use the tools provided that the teacher supervises their work. Pip first assumes that a teacher's arrival guarantees an afternoon session. Sunny points to another sentence: sessions may be canceled if essential equipment is damaged. They realize that supervision is necessary but may not be sufficient for the workshop to operate. The notice also asks students to check the daily announcement before carrying unfinished projects to the room. Pip rewrites his summary to include both the supervision condition and the possible equipment restriction.

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words explaining improvements to a fictional exhibition. Use a to-purpose phrase and a so that clause with a different subject. Connect each change to a visitor need.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，解釋虛構展覽的改善。使用 to 目的片語，以及主詞不同的 so that 子句；每項修改都要對應訪客需要。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our class revised the exhibition signs to make the route easier to follow. We placed a simple map beside the entrance so that new visitors could choose a starting point. Pip enlarged the labels so that people at the back could read them without moving forward. I checked the directions twice to prevent confusing turns. Each change responds to a particular visitor need, rather than adding decoration without a clear purpose.
practice.reading_en: Pip is helping prepare a fictional school exhibition. At first, the display labels look attractive but are difficult to read from the back of the room. He enlarges the letters so that visitors can read them without crowding around each object. Sunny places a map near the entrance to make the route easier to follow. She checks each arrow to prevent visitors from taking a wrong turn. Their explanation names both the changes and their purposes. It also distinguishes the people acting: Pip changes the labels, while visitors do the reading. A so that clause makes that different subject explicit and keeps the purpose clear.

titles.ja: バランスの取れた提案をする

objectives_zh_TW: 根據明確使用目的比較兩種可行方案。
在建議中說明優先標準與方案限制。
提出與限制對應的試辦或後續評估方法。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 結論不必宣稱某方案永遠最好。說清楚「對誰、為了什麼目的」較合適，並讓下一步回應已指出的限制。

practice.prompt_en: Write 60-90 words recommending either a lunchtime or after-school homework help desk. Compare access and meeting length, state a limitation, and propose a relevant trial.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫60–90個英文單字，建議在午餐或放學後設作業諮詢時段。比較參加方便性與討論長度，說明限制並提出對應試辦。
practice.sample_answer_en: I recommend a lunchtime homework desk for students with brief questions. Compared with an after-school session, it is easier for students who must catch early buses to attend. The main limitation is time: lunch sessions cannot support long discussions. We could therefore begin with short questions and offer separate appointments for difficult problems. During a trial, volunteers should record how many questions need another meeting. That information would show whether the proposed format fits students' needs.
practice.reading_en: A fictional student council is choosing between lunchtime and after-school homework help. An after-school desk allows longer discussions, but some students must leave immediately to catch buses. A lunchtime desk is easier for those students to attend, although each meeting would be shorter. The council decides that its first goal is to answer brief homework questions, not provide full tutoring sessions. It recommends lunchtime as a starting point and proposes a short trial. Volunteers would record whether questions can be resolved within the available time. If many require longer discussion, the council could add appointments. The recommendation connects its choice, its limitation, and a practical way to evaluate the plan.

questions.prompt_en: What is the council's first goal?
questions.answer_en: It aims to answer brief homework questions rather than provide full tutoring sessions.

questions.prompt_en: Why does it prefer lunchtime despite the shorter meetings?
questions.answer_en: Lunchtime is accessible to students who must catch early buses, and the goal is brief questions.

questions.prompt_en: What trial result would support adding appointments? Explain.
questions.answer_en: Many questions needing longer discussion would show that short lunch meetings are insufficient for those questions.

practice.prompt_en: Write a revised 60-90 word report of a fictional park cleanup. Keep the cleanup focus, use consistent past tense and three parallel past verbs, and include a clear reference to labeled bags.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 用60–90個英文單字，寫一段修訂後的虛構公園清掃報告。保持清掃焦點、過去時態一致，使用三個平行過去式動詞，並清楚提及貼好標籤的袋子。
practice.sample_answer_en: Last Saturday, our class cleaned the small park beside the river. We collected litter, labeled bags, and recorded the results before leaving. The labeled bags helped the recycling team separate different materials without opening every bag. Our teacher checked the area with us, and we removed the final pieces of paper near the gate. The activity showed us that careful organization could make a shared task easier for the next group of workers.
practice.reading_en: Sunny is revising a fictional report about a park cleanup. Her draft describes a completed event but sometimes switches into present tense. It also uses an unclear They after mentioning both students and collection bags. A sentence about her favorite music interrupts the cleanup focus. Sunny removes that sentence and uses past tense throughout the account. She writes a parallel list: the class collected litter, labeled bags, and recorded the results. Then she names The labeled bags directly to explain what helped the recycling team. Her revision keeps the event and its lesson clear instead of adding more details simply to make the report longer.

questions.prompt_en: Which irrelevant detail does Sunny remove?
questions.answer_en: She removes the sentence about her favorite music.

questions.prompt_en: Why does she replace They with The labeled bags?
questions.answer_en: The original pronoun could refer to students or bags; naming the bags makes the reference clear.

questions.prompt_en: What makes collected, labeled, and recorded a useful revision?
questions.answer_en: They are parallel past-tense verbs that consistently describe the completed cleanup activities.

practice.prompt_en: Write a 60-90 word school proposal using the fictional reading. Recommend a repair table or shelf, cite the feedback accurately, acknowledge a limitation, and propose a conditional trial with a purpose.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 根據虛構閱讀寫60–90個英文單字的校園提案。建議維修桌或置物架，準確引用回饋、承認限制，提出有條件且目的清楚的試辦。
practice.sample_answer_en: I recommend a lunchtime repair table for the art club. In the fictional class feedback, students asked for help fixing loose model parts, which a storage shelf alone cannot provide. The table would offer direct assistance, although it needs a supervising teacher and enough space. We should run a short trial provided that supervision is available. Volunteers can record unfinished repairs so that the club can judge whether lunch gives students enough time.
practice.reading_en: A fictional art class is choosing between a storage shelf and a lunchtime repair table. Its written feedback repeatedly mentions loose model parts and uncertainty about how to fix them. A shelf would protect unfinished models and require little daily attention, but it would not directly answer repair questions. A repair table would offer help, although it needs space and a supervising teacher. Sunny recommends trying the table only when supervision is available. Volunteers would record which repairs remain unfinished at the end of lunch. That record could show whether the available time is sufficient. The class feedback supports a local trial, not a claim about every student in the school.

questions.prompt_en: What problem appears in the fictional class feedback?
questions.answer_en: Students mention loose model parts and uncertainty about how to repair them.

questions.prompt_en: Why does Sunny prefer a repair table to a shelf for this problem?
questions.answer_en: A repair table offers help with fixing models, while a shelf mainly protects stored work.

questions.prompt_en: What can the trial record help evaluate, and what can it not establish?
questions.answer_en: It can help evaluate whether lunchtime is sufficient for repairs. It cannot establish what every student in the school needs.

objectives_zh_TW: 區分籠統斷言與可討論的具體主張。
以對象、行動與範圍縮小主張。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 問一句：誰要做什麼、在哪個範圍、怎樣判斷成效？具體不等於已證明，仍要提出支持。

practice.reading_en: At a fictional student council meeting, Sam opens with the statement, "School life should be better." Everyone agrees, but nobody knows what action to take. Amy suggests a narrower claim: the library should reserve a quiet study area during lunch for a short trial. Her claim identifies a place, an action, and a limited period for testing it. Another student objects that group projects also need space. Amy therefore adds that the trial should use only one corner and leave the discussion tables available. The council has not proved that her proposal will work. However, members can now discuss the same decision and choose useful evidence, such as whether students can find quiet seats without reducing group access. A precise claim makes disagreement and evaluation possible instead of merely inviting approval.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words revising a vague school improvement claim. Specify an action, scope, possible objection, and evaluation criterion.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞，將籠統的校園改善主張改得具體，交代行動、範圍、可能異議與評估標準。
practice.sample_answer_en: Saying that our school needs better breaks does not identify a decision. I propose opening one classroom for quiet reading during the afternoon break for a short trial. Students who prefer talking could continue using the courtyard. A possible objection is that supervising another room would burden teachers, so the council should first ask whether an existing duty can cover it. We could evaluate the trial by checking whether readers find usable seats and whether supervision remains manageable. This proposal is limited enough to discuss, although its benefits still need evidence.

questions.prompt_en: What specific action does Amy propose?
questions.answer_en: She proposes reserving one library corner for quiet study during a short lunchtime trial.

questions.prompt_en: Why does Amy leave the discussion tables available?
questions.answer_en: Another student explains that group projects also need space.

questions.prompt_en: Why is Amy's claim more useful than Sam's opening statement?
questions.answer_en: It names an action and a limited scope, so members can discuss access and evaluate the trial.

區分個別例子與涵蓋較廣的證明。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional school discussion, Amy argues that the library needs clearer signs. She describes a new student who walked past the history shelves while looking for a history book. The example is relevant because it concerns finding a subject area, but it cannot show how frequently the problem occurs. Sam offers a photograph of the library's attractive windows. The photograph may support a claim about the building's appearance, yet it says little about navigation. Pip suggests observing several ordinary lunch periods and recording requests for directions. Amy also wants comments from students who found books easily, so the evidence will include successful visits. The group keeps the original example as an illustration rather than presenting it as proof that every visitor gets lost. Their next task is to collect information that matches the exact claim.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words evaluating two pieces of evidence for a fictional school claim. Explain relevance, limits, and useful additional evidence.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞，評估支持虛構校園主張的兩項證據，說明相關性、限制及還需要的資料。
practice.sample_answer_en: A claim that our lunch queue needs improvement requires evidence about waiting. A student's account of missing the start of a club meeting is relevant because it describes a possible consequence of a long queue. However, one experience does not establish the usual waiting time. A photograph of colorful trays is less useful because appearance does not show how quickly students receive food. I would observe the queue on ordinary days and include short waits as well as long ones. This would help determine whether the proposed change addresses a recurring problem.

questions.prompt_en: Why is the lost student's experience relevant?
questions.answer_en: It concerns finding a subject area, which relates to the claim about clearer signs.

questions.prompt_en: Why is the window photograph weak evidence for this claim?
questions.answer_en: It concerns appearance rather than navigation.

questions.prompt_en: Would observing only confused visitors fairly test the claim? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The passage also calls for successful visits, which show whether the problem affects visitors more broadly.

objectives_zh_TW: 區分證據、推理與主張在段落中的作用。

指出推理依賴的條件，避免把關聯當保證。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 在證據後補一句「這為何與主張有關？」再找隱藏條件；解釋要增加邏輯，不是換詞重複。

practice.reading_en: A fictional reading club wants to move its meetings from the courtyard to an unused classroom. Its draft says, "The courtyard is noisy. Therefore, the classroom is better." The conclusion may be reasonable, but the draft leaves the connection unclear. Amy adds that members need to hear one another while discussing difficult passages. Noise can interrupt that exchange, so a quieter place may support the club's specific activity. She also checks whether the classroom will actually be quieter during meeting time. A music group sometimes rehearses next door, and an indoor location alone does not guarantee silence. The revised proposal recommends a trial only when the neighboring room is unused. By explaining the activity, the obstacle, and the relevant condition, the club turns a loose preference into a reasoned recommendation. It still needs to observe how the trial works.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words linking evidence to a fictional recommendation. Explain the mechanism and a condition needed for the recommendation to work.

objectives_zh_TW: 依證據強度選擇 may、likely 與 tends to。
保留人物原話的不確定性而不誇大結論。
把可能結果、較有把握的預期和反覆趨向分開。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 這些表達不是固定機率換算表；看作者有多少依據，以及談的是可能、預期還是重複模式。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional planning exercise, a club compares statements about an outdoor performance. The weather notice says rain is likely in the afternoon, so the organizer expects rain but does not treat it as certain. A student adds that the stage may become slippery. This describes a possibility; the notice does not measure the condition of the stage. Another member says outdoor rehearsals tend to need more setup time because equipment must be carried outside. She bases that general tendency on the club's previous rehearsals, while acknowledging that some were quick. Their final plan reserves an indoor room as a backup. It does not claim that the performance will definitely fail outside. By matching each statement to its basis, the members communicate useful caution without pretending that every uncertain event has the same chance of happening.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words about an uncertain fictional event. Use may, likely, and tends to with clear supporting contexts and a reasonable response.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞描述不確定的虛構活動，用明確語境支持 may、likely、tends to，並提出合理應對。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our fictional drama club is planning an outdoor rehearsal. The weather notice says strong wind is likely, so we should expect disruption without assuming it is certain. Loose pages may blow away, although we have not checked conditions at the stage. The club tends to spend longer setting up outdoors because members carry equipment from the building. That pattern has exceptions when everything is prepared in advance. I suggest keeping an indoor room available and placing scripts in folders. These steps respond to the evidence while leaving room for the event to proceed normally.

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先寫實際情況和時間，再寫假設。第二條件句的過去形不一定指過去；第三條件句回望無法重做的事件。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional debate club, members want a larger meeting room, but their current budget is too small. Amy says, "If we had more money, we would rent a larger room." Her past verb form describes an unreal situation now, not an earlier payment. The club also discusses a separate mistake. Yesterday they missed the deadline for requesting the free school hall. The rules say every request submitted on time receives consideration, but approval depends on availability. Pip says, "If we had applied earlier, our request would have received consideration." He does not claim that approval was certain. That condition imagines a different completed past. The group cannot change yesterday's submission, but it can record future deadlines. Keeping the real situation beside each conditional helps members distinguish present possibilities from reflection on an unchangeable past.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words about a fictional club. State a present limitation and a completed past mistake, then use second and third conditionals accurately.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞描述虛構社團，交代現在的限制及已發生的失誤，再正確使用第二、第三條件句。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our fictional film club has only a small budget this term. If we had more money, we would rent a room with a larger screen. This imagines a different situation now rather than describing last year's funds. We also missed yesterday's deadline for borrowing the school projector. The borrowing rules guarantee consideration for timely requests, not approval. If we had submitted our request earlier, it would have received consideration. We cannot change that missed deadline, but we can add reminders for the next event and check availability before announcing our plans.

practice.reading_en: A fictional club arrives late at a workshop because its organizer did not check a changed bus timetable. Looking back, she says, "I should have checked the schedule." She is evaluating a past choice, not claiming that she checked it. A member notes that they could have taken an earlier bus; seats were available and the group was ready before departure. In this context, could have describes an unused opportunity. Another student wonders whether road repairs delayed the bus they actually took. He says repairs might have caused the delay, but nobody has a traffic report. The group keeps this explanation uncertain instead of using it to excuse the known planning mistake. Their reflection separates what they know, what they could have done, and what remains possible. Next time, they will verify the schedule before choosing a departure.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words reflecting on a fictional missed event. Distinguish should have, an unused could have opportunity, and an uncertain might have explanation.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞回顧虛構的錯過活動事件，區分 should have 的反省、could have 的未用機會及 might have 的不確定解釋。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our fictional club missed the opening of an exhibition after leaving school late. I should have checked the starting time before announcing our departure plan. We could have left earlier because every member was ready and an earlier bus had available seats. That option existed, but we did not use it. Heavy traffic might have added to the delay, although we have no report confirming that explanation. We should not present the possibility as an established fact. For the next visit, I will verify the schedule and leave a reasonable margin for travel.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional school council, Amy proposes keeping the library open later during examination week. Sam objects that staff already have demanding schedules. His concern is workload, not a belief that students should avoid studying. Amy first summarizes his point fairly: longer opening hours could add duties unless the school changes existing arrangements. She then narrows her proposal to a short trial on afternoons when a supervised study session already takes place nearby. This adjustment may reduce additional work, but it still requires the staff's agreement. Sam accepts that the revision addresses part of his concern and asks who will handle closing the room. The discussion has not ended in complete agreement. Nevertheless, it has moved from defending positions to examining practical conditions. A fair counterargument helps the proposal become more workable instead of merely making the opponent look unreasonable.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words proposing a fictional change. State a fair counterargument, acknowledge its force, and offer a response with an unresolved condition.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞提出虛構改變，公平描述反方理由、承認其重要性，並提出有待確認條件的回應。
practice.sample_answer_en: Our club should offer an introductory workshop for new members. A reasonable objection is that experienced students already spend considerable time preparing regular meetings. This concern deserves attention; it does not mean those students oppose welcoming newcomers. I suggest using an existing meeting for a short introduction rather than adding another event. New members could then choose which later activities to attend. This would limit additional preparation, although someone would still need to organize the introductory materials. Before adopting the plan, we should ask whether volunteers can take that task without losing time for their own projects.

questions.prompt_en: Why is claiming that Sam opposes studying an unfair response?

objectives_zh_TW: 依說話行動選擇 suggests、reports、argues 等轉述動詞。
改寫時保留原文範圍、條件與不確定程度。
識別把 may 改成 will 或把建議寫成證明的失真。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先記下作者做了什麼：回報觀察、提出建議還是主張理由。換詞時不可順便提高確定度。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional planning memo, the librarian writes, "A short trial may reveal whether students use the room after lunch." Amy summarizes this as a suggestion to test demand. Sam's first summary says the librarian proves that afternoon access will improve learning. That version changes both the strength and the topic of the original statement. The memo discusses possible information about room use, not demonstrated learning gains. Elsewhere, the librarian reports that some visitors asked about later access. Reporting this observation is different from arguing that the entire schedule should change. The club revises its summary to keep these actions separate: the librarian reports requests and suggests a limited trial. Members can still add their own recommendation, but they must label it as their response. Accurate reporting preserves the source's uncertainty even when a stronger statement would make the proposal easier to sell.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words reporting this fictional note: "Longer breaks may help some students settle before class. A trial is worth considering." Preserve its limits, then separate your response.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞轉述虛構便條：「較長休息可能幫助部分學生在課前安定下來，值得考慮試辦。」保留限制，再區分自己的回應。
practice.sample_answer_en: The fictional note suggests considering a trial of longer breaks. It states that additional time may help some students settle before class, rather than claiming that every student will learn more. The wording presents a possibility and limits the group that might benefit. It does not report a completed experiment or establish the ideal break length. My response is that a trial could be useful if teachers and students agree on what to observe. We should examine transitions into lessons and possible scheduling difficulties before recommending a permanent change.

practice.reading_en: For a fictional class exercise, students receive a short note by librarian Maya Chen titled "Shared Study Space." The note states, "Quiet areas help some readers concentrate, but discussion areas serve a different purpose." Amy quotes only the first clause and correctly marks the exact words with quotation marks. However, her paragraph then implies that the note supports removing every discussion table. That interpretation ignores the balancing clause. Pip instead paraphrases the whole idea: Chen recognizes separate uses for quiet and conversational spaces. He names the author and note so readers can identify the source provided in class. Pip then adds his own analysis, arguing that a trial should preserve both functions. The exercise does not require invented publication details or outside research. Its aim is to distinguish the source's words, the student's paraphrase, and the student's independent conclusion while keeping the original balance visible.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words responding to Maya Chen's fictional note in the reading. Include one exact short quotation, an attributed paraphrase, and your separate recommendation.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞回應閱讀中 Maya Chen 的虛構便條，包含一段準確短引文、注明來源的改寫與自己獨立的建議。
practice.sample_answer_en: In the fictional note "Shared Study Space," Maya Chen writes, "Quiet areas help some readers concentrate." The rest of her sentence also recognizes the purpose of discussion areas. In other words, Chen presents these spaces as serving different needs rather than declaring one useful and the other unnecessary. My recommendation is to preserve discussion tables while testing a clearly marked quiet corner. That response follows from the note's balance, but the specific trial is my proposal. We would still need information about available space and actual use before deciding whether the arrangement should continue.

questions.prompt_en: What makes Pip's attribution and response more responsible?
questions.answer_en: He identifies the provided author and note, preserves both functions, and labels his own recommendation as analysis.

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 每個百分比旁都要想「多少人中的多少人？」未回覆不是反對；小樣本的結果也不是全校民意。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional class survey, twenty students answered a question about the library's schedule. Twelve chose longer afternoon hours, five preferred an earlier opening, and three chose no change. Each respondent selected one option. The twelve supporters therefore represent sixty percent of the respondents, not sixty percent of the whole school. The class has twenty-five students, so five classmates did not answer. Their views are unknown; they should not automatically be counted as opponents of longer hours. The question also asked for a preferred schedule, not how often respondents would actually visit. Amy reports these limits beside the results. She concludes that longer afternoon access was the most popular option among those who replied and recommends checking likely use before proposing a permanent change. The fictional numbers support a careful description of this group, but they cannot establish what every student needs.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words reporting this hypothetical survey: 18 responses from a class of 24; 9 prefer a quiet room, 6 a discussion room, 3 no change. Explain one limit and a next step.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞報告假設問卷：全班24人，18人回覆；9人選安靜室、6人選討論室、3人選不改變。說明一項限制與下一步。
practice.sample_answer_en: In this hypothetical class survey, eighteen of twenty-four students responded. Nine respondents preferred a quiet room, six chose a discussion room, and three wanted no change. Half of the respondents therefore selected the quiet room, but that is not half of the entire school. The preferences of the six classmates who did not reply remain unknown. The question also does not show how often either room would be used. Before recommending a permanent arrangement, the class should invite the missing responses and ask when students would actually need each type of space.

questions.prompt_en: How many respondents chose longer afternoon hours?
questions.answer_en: Twelve of the twenty respondents chose that option.

questions.prompt_en: Why should the five nonrespondents not be counted as opponents?
questions.answer_en: They did not answer, so their preferences are unknown.

questions.prompt_en: Would the survey prove that sixty percent of the school will use longer hours? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The denominator is respondents in one class, and the question measured preference rather than actual use.

objectives_zh_TW: 區分一起變動的現象與已證明的因果。
找出比較中同時改變的其他條件。
提出有助排除替代解釋且符合範圍的下一步。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 看到「之後變好」先問還有什麼改了；承認資料有價值，同時把觀察結果和原因推論分開。

practice.reading_en: In a hypothetical class project, a study club records eight visitors during one lunchtime session and fourteen during the next. A new sign appeared before the second session, so the organizer claims that the sign caused the increase. However, other conditions also changed. The first session took place during a sports competition, while the second was held before a major assignment deadline. The club did not ask visitors why they came. The increase is real within the fictional records, but its cause is unresolved. A sign may have helped, yet the timetable and assignment could also explain the difference. Amy recommends observing more sessions under similar conditions and asking visitors how they learned about the club. These steps would strengthen the comparison without guaranteeing a perfect experiment. The appropriate conclusion is that attendance increased after the sign appeared, not that the sign alone produced the increase.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words evaluating a hypothetical claim: attendance rose from 10 to 16 after an email reminder, but the room and meeting day also changed. Give a cautious conclusion and next step.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞評估假設主張：寄出提醒信後，出席由10人增至16人，但地點和日期也改了。提出審慎結論與下一步。
practice.sample_answer_en: In these hypothetical records, attendance increased from ten students to sixteen after an email reminder was sent. The timing is consistent with a helpful reminder, but it does not prove that the email caused the increase. The room and meeting day also changed, so greater convenience might explain some of the difference. We should report the increase without assigning its entire cause to one factor. For a stronger comparison, the club could keep the room and day similar across later meetings and ask visitors whether the reminder influenced their decision to attend.

questions.prompt_en: How did attendance change in the hypothetical records?
questions.answer_en: It rose from eight visitors to fourteen.

questions.prompt_en: Name two other conditions that could explain the change.
questions.answer_en: The sports competition affected the first session, and an assignment deadline preceded the second.

questions.prompt_en: Why is caused stronger than the evidence supports?
questions.answer_en: Several conditions changed and visitors' reasons were not collected, so the sign's independent effect is unknown.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional class survey, fifteen of twenty-four respondents support a quiet reading room during lunch. Six prefer a discussion room, and three want no change. The council considers a proposal to test a quiet room on days when an unused classroom and existing supervision are available. Supporters argue that a separate room could reduce interruptions for readers. A fair objection is that discussion groups must not lose their only meeting space. The revised plan therefore keeps their room open and uses another space for the trial. Survey preferences do not prove that students will attend, and the respondents represent one class rather than the whole school. The council recommends recording actual use and asking both readers and discussion groups about access. Its conclusion supports a limited trial under stated conditions, not a permanent change based solely on a small survey.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words responding to the fictional survey in the reading. Give a qualified claim, evidence, reasoning, a fair objection, and a condition for your recommendation.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞回應短文的虛構問卷，提出有限定的主張、證據、解釋、公平異議及建議成立的條件。
practice.sample_answer_en: The council should test a quiet reading room when suitable space and supervision are available. In the fictional survey, fifteen of twenty-four respondents preferred this option, suggesting interest within that class. A separate room could reduce interruptions for readers, which explains why the preference is relevant. However, discussion groups reasonably worry about losing access. Their current room should remain available during the trial. Preferences do not guarantee attendance or represent the whole school. The council should therefore record actual use and seek feedback from both groups before deciding whether the arrangement deserves a longer trial.

objectives_zh_TW: 比較公告、邀請和評論如何處理同一活動。

episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 先找讀者被要求做什麼，以及哪些資訊最突出；標題和形式有幫助，但仍要用內文確認目的。

practice.reading_en: A fictional school exhibition appears in three short texts. An official notice tells visitors that the entrance has moved to the east gate while repairs continue. It asks them to follow the marked path and gives the opening time. A club invitation describes student artwork and encourages families to attend the opening afternoon. It also asks guests to reply so organizers can prepare seats. A student commentary argues that the exhibition should include unfinished work as well as polished pieces, because visitors could then understand the creative process. Although all three texts concern the same event, they direct attention toward different decisions. The notice supports safe arrival, the invitation seeks participation, and the commentary invites judgment about display choices. Readers should use wording and requested actions to identify purpose rather than assuming that every text about an exhibition simply advertises it.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words as a fictional invitation to a school exhibition. Address families, explain the event, request a reply, and distinguish your purpose from a safety notice.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞，撰寫給家庭的虛構校展邀請，介紹活動、請對方回覆，並說明與安全公告不同的目的。
practice.sample_answer_en: Dear families, our art club warmly invites you to the opening of its fictional school exhibition next Friday afternoon. Students will explain how their sketches developed into finished work, and visitors can ask about the choices behind each piece. Please reply to the club before Thursday so we can arrange enough seats for the discussion. Our aim is to encourage participation and conversation about student creativity. A separate entrance notice will explain the safe route through the building while repairs continue. We look forward to hearing your questions and sharing the work with you.

questions.prompt_en: What practical change does the official notice explain?
questions.answer_en: Visitors must use the east gate while repairs continue.

questions.prompt_en: Why does the invitation ask guests to reply?
questions.answer_en: Organizers need to prepare seats.

questions.prompt_en: Why would calling the commentary an entrance notice misrepresent its purpose?
questions.answer_en: It argues for displaying unfinished work rather than giving arrival instructions.

objectives_zh_TW: 辨認跨段落的主張、證據、解釋與回應。
說明例子在整體論證中的用途。
追蹤異議如何改變結論條件。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 替每段寫作用而不是只寫主題，例如「提出限制」。再檢查結論是否真的回應中間出現的顧慮。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional school newsletter, the opening paragraph recommends a supervised bicycle repair desk. The writer says students sometimes arrive with loose seats or flat tires and do not know where to seek basic help. These examples explain the need, but they do not show how many students would use the desk. The next paragraph acknowledges an objection: enthusiastic volunteers may lack the training to repair safety-critical parts. Instead of dismissing the concern, the writer restricts the proposed desk to simple checks and directs complex repairs to qualified adults. The final paragraph recommends a short trial only if a trained supervisor is available. The argument therefore moves from a need to a proposal, then through a limitation to a conditional conclusion. A reader who notices only the opening recommendation would miss the safeguards that determine what the writer actually supports.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words mapping the fictional repair-desk argument. Identify the claim, illustrative evidence, objection, response, and condition in the final conclusion.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞分析虛構維修站論證，指出主張、例證、異議、回應及結論中的條件。
practice.sample_answer_en: The newsletter initially recommends a supervised bicycle repair desk. Examples of loose seats and flat tires explain why help might be useful, although they do not measure total demand. The second part introduces a safety objection: volunteers may not have enough training for complex repairs. The writer responds by limiting the desk's tasks and referring difficult work to qualified adults. Finally, the recommendation depends on having a trained supervisor. This condition matters because the article supports a controlled trial, not unrestricted repairs. Following the paragraph roles prevents readers from overstating the opening claim.

questions.prompt_en: What service does the opening paragraph recommend?
questions.answer_en: A supervised bicycle repair desk.

questions.prompt_en: What role do the loose seats and flat tires play?
questions.answer_en: They illustrate students' need for help, but do not establish demand across the school.

questions.prompt_en: Would an unsupervised desk handling all repairs match the final argument? Explain.
questions.answer_en: No. The proposal limits tasks, refers complex repairs to qualified adults, and requires a trained supervisor.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional club email, the organizer writes, "Thank you for sending the draft. Several labels are still missing, and the printer needs the file tomorrow. Could you add them this afternoon?" The opening is polite, while the details create urgency. The message does not praise the draft as complete, but it also does not accuse the recipient of being careless. A classmate rewrites the request as, "You obviously ignored the instructions again." This version adds blame that the original wording does not establish. Another classmate interprets the word still as proof of anger. Yet still can simply mark an unfinished task, and the surrounding request remains specific and cooperative. A careful reading describes the original tone as polite but concerned about time. The club learns to support tone judgments with several contextual clues rather than assigning an emotion from one isolated word.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words rewriting a fictional accusatory message into a cooperative request. Preserve missing labels and tomorrow's printing deadline, then explain two wording choices.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞，將虛構指責訊息改成合作式請求，保留缺少標籤與明天印刷期限，並解釋兩項用字選擇。
practice.sample_answer_en: Thank you for sending the exhibition draft. Several picture labels are still missing, and the printer needs the completed file tomorrow morning. Could you add the labels this afternoon and let me know if you need any details from the artists? This will help us prepare the final version on time. In this revision, the thanks recognizes work already done without pretending the file is complete. The offer of information makes cooperation possible. Neither choice removes the deadline, but both avoid accusing the recipient of deliberately ignoring instructions when the message provides no evidence of that intention.

practice.reading_en: In a fictional committee meeting, Mina enters after the chair has finished explaining the budget. She looks at a revised spreadsheet and asks why the equipment allowance is smaller than in yesterday's draft. The chair offers to summarize the earlier discussion during the break. These details suggest that Mina missed at least part of the budget explanation. They do not show why she arrived at that moment. A reader might imagine that she overslept, but the passage says nothing about her journey or earlier duties. Her question also shows that she noticed a change; it does not support a claim that she ignored the documents completely. The useful inference is limited to what she may need now: an explanation of the revision. Before judging her preparation or commitment, the committee would need information that this scene does not provide.

practice.sample_answer_en: The scene does not establish that Mina was unprepared. She enters after the budget explanation, and the chair offers to summarize the earlier discussion. These details suggest that she may need information presented before her arrival. However, she notices that the equipment allowance differs from yesterday's draft, which shows attention to at least one document change. A narrower conclusion is that she probably missed part of the explanation and wants to understand the revision. We still do not know why she arrived then or what other preparation she completed before the meeting.

titles.ja: 指示関係とつながりを追う

objectives_zh_TW: 找出代名詞指向的人物或物件。
解讀 this 加概括名詞所指的整段事件。
以詞彙連結與必要重述改善含糊指代。
episodes.parent_tip_zh_TW: 不只往前找最近名詞；this delay 等組合常概括整件事。先確認句意，再比對單複數與詞彙鏈。

practice.reading_en: In a fictional exhibition project, a supplier warns the art club that its paper delivery will arrive late because the loading area is closed. This delay forces the club to postpone printing, but it does not change the exhibition date. Amy contacts the supplier and asks for an updated arrival time. She then sends the schedule to Pip, who adjusts the printing plan. The new timetable leaves less time for checking labels, so this reduction concerns the teacher supervising the display. Here, this delay summarizes the late delivery, while this reduction refers to the smaller amount of checking time. Neither expression points merely to the closest single noun. Words such as schedule, plan, and timetable also help connect related information across sentences. Repeating delivery or checking time when necessary can make a revision clearer than adding another vague it.
practice.prompt_en: Write 80-110 words explaining the delivery problem. Use one clear pronoun, this delay, and another summary noun, then clarify any potentially ambiguous reference.
practice.prompt_zh_TW: 寫80至110詞說明送貨問題，使用一個明確代名詞、this delay 及另一個概括名詞，並釐清可能含糊的指代。
practice.sample_answer_en: The supplier tells Amy that the paper delivery will arrive late because the loading area is closed. This delay means the art club must postpone printing. Amy asks for the revised arrival time, and she passes the answer to Pip. He changes the printing timetable, leaving less time for checking the labels. This reduction worries the supervising teacher because errors may be missed. To keep the message clear, the final note repeats checking time instead of referring to the problem simply as it. The repeated phrase identifies the particular consequence that needs attention.

questions.prompt_en: What does this reduction refer to?
questions.answer_en: It refers to the smaller amount of time available for checking labels.

questions.prompt_en: Why would replacing this reduction with it reduce clarity?
questions.answer_en: The passage contains several possible singular references, while the summary noun identifies the specific change in checking time.
